back: $p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\pi_k\mathcal N(x\mid\mu_k,\Sigma_k)$ with $\pi_k\ge0$, $\sum_k\pi_k=1$. Multimodal; $K=1$ is a single Gaussian.
Hidden one-hot $z$ with $p(z_k=1)=\pi_k$ and $x\mid z_k=1\sim\mathcal N(\mu_k,\Sigma_k)$. Marginalising $z$ gives the mixture. Sampling: draw $k$, then draw $x$ (ancestral sampling).
$r_{nk}=\dfrac{\pi_k\mathcal N(x_n\mid\mu_k,\Sigma_k)}{\sum_j\pi_j\mathcal N(x_n\mid\mu_j,\Sigma_j)}=p(z_{nk}=1\mid x_n)$: Bayes' theorem with prior $\pi_k$.
$\mu_k=\frac1{N_k}\sum_nr_{nk}x_n$: responsibility-weighted average of all points. From $\sum_nr_{nk}\Sigma_k^{-1}(x_n-\mu_k)=0$.
$\Sigma_k=\frac1{N_k}\sum_nr_{nk}(x_n-\mu_k)(x_n-\mu_k)^\top$, using the new $\mu_k$. In 1-D: weighted variance.
$\pi_k=N_k/N$, from a Lagrange multiplier for $\sum_k\pi_k=1$ (which turns out to be $\lambda=-N$).

front: Why no closed-form MLE for a GMM?
back: The log of a sum, $\log\sum_k\pi_k\mathcal N(\cdot)$, does not split per component; the stationarity equations contain responsibilities that depend on all parameters, so they are solved iteratively.

front: Why does EM increase the log-likelihood?
back: Jensen gives $\ell(\theta)\ge F(q,\theta)$, tight when $q$ equals the posterior. E-step makes it tight at $\theta^{(t)}$; M-step raises $F$; so $\ell(\theta^{(t+1)})\ge F\ge\ell(\theta^{(t)})$.
$Q(\theta)=\sum_{n,k}r_{nk}[\log\pi_k+\log\mathcal N(x_n\mid\mu_k,\Sigma_k)]$: expected complete-data log-likelihood. The M-step maximises it with $r$ fixed.

front: k-means as a limit of EM
back: Equal weights, shared spherical covariance $\sigma^2I$, $\sigma^2\to0$: responsibilities become 0/1 (nearest centre) and the M-step is the cluster mean.

A component centred on one data point with $\sigma^2\to0$ makes the likelihood diverge ($1/\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}$). Add a variance floor $\varepsilon I$, re-initialise collapsing components, or use a prior.
Results depend on the start (local maxima). Use several random restarts, or k-means: centres as $\mu_k$, cluster covariances as $\Sigma_k$, cluster fractions as $\pi_k$.
Permuting the $K$ components gives the same density ($K!$ equivalent solutions), so component indices carry no intrinsic meaning.
$\log\sum_ke^{a_k}=m+\log\sum_ke^{a_k-m}$ with $m=\max_ka_k$. Compute responsibilities and the log-likelihood in logs to avoid underflow.
